templates.readme:
# ClickHouse

The open-source column-oriented database for real-time analytics: SQL over
billions of rows in milliseconds, with compression that keeps the disk small.

## What gets deployed

| Service | Image | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **ClickHouse** | `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.8.27.9` (LTS) | Public HTTP interface. Data on a 10 GB volume |

## After deploy

Your URL serves ClickHouse's **HTTP interface** over HTTPS. Sign in as
`default` with the password from the deploy form:

- **In the browser**: open `https://<your-url>/play` for the built-in SQL
  console.
- **From code**: any HTTP client, e.g. Python's `clickhouse-connect`:
  ```python
  import clickhouse_connect
  client = clickhouse_connect.get_client(host="<your-url>", port=443, secure=True,
                                         username="default", password="…")
  ```
- **curl**:
  ```bash
  curl -u default:… https://<your-url>/ --data-binary "SELECT version()"
  ```

`default` can manage access: create a user per app with `CREATE USER … IDENTIFIED BY …`
and `GRANT`.

## Good to know

- Only the HTTP interface is exposed. The native TCP protocol (port 9000,
  used by `clickhouse-client`) is not reachable from outside. Use
  `clickhouse-client` from inside the project, or an HTTP client.
- Changing `CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD` and redeploying changes the `default` user's
  password.
- ClickHouse uses up to 90% of the memory it is given. 2 GB or more is
  comfortable for real workloads.

Turns a SQL database into an instant REST and GraphQL API, with a no-code app
to manage content, users, files and permissions.

Directus uses the Business Source License: it is free for organizations under

anything beyond that.

# Ghost

A professional publishing platform: a modern editor, newsletters, paid
memberships and themes.

## What gets deployed

| Service | Image | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Ghost** | `ghost:6.70.0` | Public. 1 GiB volume for themes, images and uploads |
| **db** | MySQL 8 | Internal. Posts, members and settings |

## After deploy

Go to `<your-url>/ghost` and create the **owner account**. The first visitor to
that page gets it, so do this right away.

## Notes

- **Email.** Staff invites, password resets and newsletters need an SMTP or
  Mailgun account. Ghost reads its config from lowercase variables, so add yours
  to the `export …` line of the service's start command, e.g.
  `mail__transport=SMTP mail__options__host=…`.
- **Custom domain.** Ghost builds every link from its `url`. After you add a
  domain, set `GHOST_URL` to it and redeploy.

templates.readme:
# Metabase

Open-source business intelligence: connect your databases, ask questions with
a visual query builder or SQL, and share dashboards with your team.

## What gets deployed

| Service | Image | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Metabase** | `metabase/metabase:v0.64.2.3` | Public. Database drivers on a 1 GB volume |
| **db** | PostgreSQL 16 | Internal. Metabase's own data: users, questions, dashboards |

## After deploy

Metabase takes a minute or two to start the first time. Then sign in with the
**admin email and password** you entered in the deploy form: the template
completes Metabase's setup with them on first boot, so the "create the first
admin" page is never open to whoever finds your URL first.

Add the databases you want to analyze under **Admin → Databases → Add a
database**. A sample database is included to play with.

## Good to know

- The password must have at least **15 characters** and not be a common
  one. If Metabase rejects it, the container stops and logs why: redeploy with a
  better password.
- `ADMIN_EMAIL` and `ADMIN_PASSWORD` are only used on first boot. Change them
  later in Metabase under **Account settings**.
- `MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY` is generated at deploy and encrypts the
  credentials of the databases you connect. Don't change it.
- Metabase is a Java app: the service starts with **1.5 GB of memory and 1
  CPU**. Raise it in the service settings for large datasets or many users.

# n8n

Workflow automation you host yourself: connect 400+ apps and APIs, run code
steps, and build AI agents on a visual canvas.

## What gets deployed

| Service | Image | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **n8n** | `n8nio/n8n:2.44.1` | Public. Editor, webhooks and the API on one URL. 1 GiB volume for credentials files and community nodes |
| **db** | PostgreSQL 16 | Internal. Workflows, executions and users |

`N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is generated for you. Every credential n8n stores is
encrypted with it, so **don't change or delete it**. If you lose it, the stored
credentials become unreadable.

## After deploy

1. Open the service URL. n8n asks you to create the **owner account**, and the
   first person to open the URL gets it, so do this right away.
2. Webhook URLs already point at the public address (`WEBHOOK_URL`). If you
   add a custom domain, update `WEBHOOK_URL` and `N8N_EDITOR_BASE_URL` to match.

## Notes

- Schedule and polling triggers run inside the n8n process, so keep the
  service running if you rely on them.
- Large workflows can need more memory. Raise the limit in the service's
  **Scale** tab.

templates.readme:
# Outline

A fast, collaborative knowledge base for your team: nested documents,
real-time editing, Markdown shortcuts, search, and integrations with Slack,
Figma, Linear and more.

## What gets deployed

| Service | Image | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Outline** | `outlinewiki/outline:1.11.0` | Public. Migrations run on boot. Uploads on a 5 GB volume |
| **db** | PostgreSQL 16 | Internal. Documents, users, history |
| **redis** | Redis 7 | Internal. Real-time collaboration and background jobs |

## Before you deploy: email

Outline signs people in with a **link sent by email**, so it needs an SMTP
server. Any transactional provider works (Resend, Postmark, Amazon SES,
Mailgun, your own). Have the host, port, credentials, and a verified sender
address ready for the deploy form.

## After deploy

The template creates the workspace on first boot with the **admin email** from
the deploy form, so nobody else can claim it. Open your Outline URL, enter that
email, and click the link you receive.

Invite your team from **Settings → Members**. To sign in with Google, Slack,
Microsoft or any OIDC provider instead of email links, add that provider's
variables (see [Outline's docs](https://docs.getoutline.com/s/hosting/doc/authentication-7ViKRmRY5o)).

## Good to know

- If Outline rejects the admin email or workspace name, the container stops and
  logs why, so the "create workspace" page never sits open. Fix the value and
  redeploy.
- `ADMIN_EMAIL`, `ADMIN_NAME` and `WORKSPACE_NAME` are only used on first boot.
- No sign-in email? Check the Outline service's logs: SMTP errors show up there.
  Port 465 needs `SMTP_SECURE=true`; 587 needs `false`.

templates.readme:
# Paperclip

Open-source orchestration for teams of AI agents. Set a company goal, hire
agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode or any HTTP/bash agent) into an
org chart, give them budgets, and track their work as tickets, all from one
dashboard.

## What gets deployed

| Service | Image | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Paperclip** | `ghcr.io/paperclipai/paperclip:2026.1012.0` | Public. Migrations run on boot. 10 GB volume for agent workspaces and data |
| **db** | PostgreSQL 16 | Internal. Companies, agents, tickets, budgets |

It runs in Paperclip's `authenticated` + `public` mode: everything requires
signing in.

## After deploy: claim the instance

Public Paperclip instances get their first admin through a **one-time invite
link**, not a setup page anyone could reach first:

1. Open the **Paperclip service's logs** and find the line
   `Claim this Paperclip instance (valid 72 hours): https://…/invite/pcp_bootstrap_…`.
2. Open that link, create your account, and accept the invite. You are now the
   instance admin.
3. Create your first company and hire agents.

The link works once. If it expires before you use it, restart the service: a new
one is printed (and the old one stops working). Once the instance has an
admin, nothing is printed.

## Good to know

- **Agents need model credentials.** Add your Anthropic, OpenAI or other API
  keys in Paperclip. They are encrypted with a key generated at deploy.
  Sign-ins made by the bundled CLIs are kept on the volume.
- Agents run **inside this container**, with its CPU and memory. The service
  starts with **2 GB and 1 CPU** (2 GB is the most memory a service can have). That is
  enough for a few agents at a time; upstream recommends 4 GB for more.
- Anyone who finds the URL can create an account, but an account sees nothing
  until an admin invites it to a company.

templates.readme:
# Umami

Simple, fast, privacy-focused web analytics: pageviews, referrers, devices,
events, funnels and goals, with no cookies and nothing sent to third parties.

## What gets deployed

| Service | Image | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Umami** | `ghcr.io/umami-software/umami:3.4.0` | Public. Migrations run on boot |
| **db** | PostgreSQL 16 | Internal. Websites, users and every event |

## After deploy

Sign in with username **`admin`** and the **password you entered in the deploy
form**. Umami ships with `admin` / `umami`; the template replaces that password
on first boot, before your URL starts answering, so the default never works on
your instance.

Then add a website under **Settings → Websites → Add website** and paste its
tracking code into your site's `<head>`:

```html
<script defer src="https://<your-umami-url>/script.js" data-website-id="…"></script>
```

## Good to know

- `ADMIN_PASSWORD` is only applied while the account still has the default
  password. Changing it later in the deploy form does nothing: change it in
  Umami under **Profile → Change password**.
- Ad blockers often block `script.js`. Umami's docs explain how to
  [rename the tracker](https://umami.is/docs/environment-variables) with
  `TRACKER_SCRIPT_NAME` if that matters to you.

templates.readme:
# Vaultwarden

A lightweight server that speaks the Bitwarden API, so the official Bitwarden
apps, browser extensions and CLI work against it.

## What gets deployed

| Service | Image | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Vaultwarden** | `vaultwarden/server:1.37.4` | Public. 1 GiB volume for the vault database (SQLite), attachments and keys |

## After deploy

1. Open the URL and **create your account**.
2. Turn off public signups: set `SIGNUPS_ALLOWED` to `false` in the service's
   variables and redeploy.
3. In any Bitwarden app, pick **Self-hosted** and enter the service URL as the
   server.

The admin panel lives at `/admin`, behind the `ADMIN_TOKEN` you chose at
deploy. Service variables are write-only, so keep a copy: to change it, set a
new `ADMIN_TOKEN` and redeploy. Deleting the variable turns the panel off.

## Notes

Vaultwarden is an independent project, not affiliated with Bitwarden, Inc.
Back up the volume: it is your vault.
